S7 Help & feedback

english: Report a problem, send feedback, common questions
Something wrong in a study, devotional, plan or the app
How do I read and move between verses?

Swipe up for the next verse and down for the previous one. Tap the book name at the top to jump to a book and chapter; “Continue” picks up where you left off in that book. Double-tap a verse to like it, or press and hold to copy it.
Where do my likes and notes go?
Use the heart and note buttons beside a verse. Everything you like, bookmark or write is in Home → Your library, and it’s saved on this phone only.

The World English Bible (WEB) and the King James Version (KJV) are built in and work offline. Tap the translation name at the top of the feed to switch. Verse actions → Compare versions shows a verse in every translation.
What does “AI-assisted” mean on a study?

Each study was written once with help from an AI model, using openly licensed sources (original-language word data and cross-reference lists) that are named at the end of the study. Every study is checked automatically, and studies marked “reviewed by a person” were also read by someone. Nothing is generated while you read. To turn studies off, go to Settings → General → Hide AI studies. If something looks wrong, use Report a problem.
How do I keep my data when I change phones?

If Google backup is turned on in your phone’s settings, Android may restore your notes, likes, plans and settings on a new phone. To be sure, go to Settings → Data & backup → Export my data, move the file to the new phone and choose Import there.
How do reminders and the widget work?

Turn on a daily reminder and pick its time in Settings → Notifications. For the home screen widget, open Verse actions on any verse and choose Set as widget verse; you can keep that verse or show the Verse of the Day, which changes just after midnight.
What do you know about me?

Nothing. There’s no account, no ads and no analytics. Your notes, likes and settings stay on your phone. The app only goes online to download study and devotional files, without anything that identifies you. Reports and feedback are emails you send yourself, so we only see your email address if you send one.

english: We don’t track you. There’s no account, no ads and no analytics, and the app contains no tracking or crash-reporting code. This page explains what the app keeps on your phone and the few things that leave it.
Your notes, likes, bookmarks, reading plans, reading progress, streak, Community vote and settings are stored in the app on this phone. We can’t see them.

Content downloads: when the app downloads studies, devotionals or the Discover and Community lists, it requests files from our content server, which Google hosts (Firebase Hosting). The requests contain no account or device ID, but like any internet request they show your IP address to Google.

Community vote: if you vote, the app sends “+1 for this ministry this month” to a counter hosted by Google (Cloud Firestore). It carries no account or device ID, and the counter stores only a number, but Google sees your IP address with the request. Showing the totals works the same way. Your own choice stays on your phone.

Emails you choose to send: Report a problem and Send feedback open your own email app with a message you can read and change first. Nothing is sent unless you send it. If you do, we see your email address and what you wrote, and we may use it to correct the content.
Links you open: a ministry’s Website and Give directly buttons open its page in your browser. That site’s own privacy policy applies. The app handles no money.
What Android and Google Play do

If backup is turned on in your phone’s settings, Android may save a copy of your notes, plans and settings to your own Google account. On Android 12 and later, the app allows this only when Android can encrypt the backup end to end, which needs a screen lock. If you use Export my data, the file goes wherever you save it.
If you let your phone share usage and diagnostics with Google, Google Play may send us crash statistics. The app has no crash-reporting code of its own.

Uninstalling the app, or clearing its data, deletes everything it stored on this phone. A backup in your Google account follows your Google account settings. Community votes can’t be deleted because they aren’t linked to anyone. To ask us to delete an email you sent, write to us.
